newsitem.title: UGANDA: Rebel-hit Ugandan town faces food - medical crises.
newsitem.headline: Rebel-hit Ugandan town faces food - medical crises.

text.p: A United Nations relief convoy under military escort on Thursday headed for the western Uganda town of Bundibugyo which is short of food and medical supplies after hit-and-run rebel attacks.
Bundibugyo, a remote town at the foot of the Ruwenzori mountains, has been cut off from the rest of the east African country for over 10 days by rebel activity, officials said.
Local government official Edward Masiga said Bundibugyo only had food supplies enough to last four to five days.

"I would estimate that there is four to five days food in town, unless the population can reach their fields to find food," said Masiga. "But right now, it's not safe to go more than 1,000 metres from the town centre.

The rebels of the Moslem-based Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacked the usually sleepy town from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo and on-off fighting with government troops has displaced over 30,000 people.
The latest humanitarian crisis has placed further strain on a country already reeling from a food shortage mainly because of drought and insecurity in the northern part of Uganda.
"There is a food shortage in Uganda as a whole," said Michael Jones, World Food Programme (WFP) deputy country director for Uganda on Thursday.

"In Bundibugyo it is impossible to estimate the number of displaced people, to tell them from local population and available food is limited. We are trying to get 60 tonnes of maize and cereals through today under military escort," he added.

The only road between Bundibugyo and the town of Fort Portal has been rendered impassable by the fighting and the government of former guerrilla leader Yoweri Museveni has had to use helicopters to reach Bundibugyo.

Lieutenant-Colonel Charles Angina, a senior army officer involved in operations against the ADF, told reporters the rag-tag rebel band was still active around Bundibugyo despite government army efforts to repulse them.

"There is a rebel movement around Bundibugyo. There was an ambush yesterday around (village of) Kirindi against the army, the rebels are all in the hills between the town and the (Congo) border," Angina said.

The latest conflict has also put pressure on the ill-equipped local hospital. Aid officials told Reuters that although Bundibugyo hospital had four qualified doctors, it desperately needed medical supplies.
Between 80 and 100 civilians are estimated to have been killed in the fighting during the last 11 days, according to local residents, military sources and the local hospitals.
At least 35 Ugandan soldiers have been wounded and more than 10 killed in latest guerrilla warfare.
Between 15 and 20 rebels have been killed, and local officials say up to 38,000 people displaced..

The Ugandan government accuses Sudan's Islamic-backed military junta of supporting the rebels in a campaign to destabilise the country. Khartoum denies the charge and in turn accuses Uganda of backing southern rebels.
